chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Shihāb ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he performed wudu (ablution), would not allow anyone to pour water for him. So it was said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, why do you not let them pour water for you?” He said: “I do not like to make anyone a شریک in my salat (prayer).”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.أُشْرِكَ: to involve or associate another in the act
key_terms.صَلَاتِي: my salat (prayer), meaning the worship connected to ritual purification

ai.seo_question: Why did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام dislike others pouring water for his wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in performing wudu (ablution) independently without allowing others to pour water for him. It highlights an attitude of sincerity, personal devotion, and care that acts connected to salat (prayer) remain personally undertaken.
